findings.problem: get_instance resolves the requester with `requester = _people(repo, [rid])[rid]`, an unguarded subscript. `_people` filters on `identity_membership` (`AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM identity_membership m WHERE m.org_id=%(org_id)s AND m.identity_id=i.id)`), so a requester who has since left the organization produces an empty mapping and `[rid]` raises KeyError, so every read of that document's approval (inbox, decision panel, instance history all route through get_instance/instances_for) 500s. In the same file `notify_outcome` (line 448) looks up the same requester with `emails_by_id(...).get(requester_id)` and degrades to an absent recipient; and the name-plumbing in this same diff adds `emails.get(x, "(removed user)")` fallbacks in decisions.py, delegation.py, explain.py, and inbox.py. Only the requester path was left unguarded.
findings.fix: Resolve the requester the way the sibling paths do: use a `.get(...)` with a `"(removed user)"` / None fallback (e.g. reuse `emails_by_id`/`names_by_id`, or guard `_people`), so a removed requester renders an attribution fallback instead of raising.

findings.problem: Two membership notions coexist under different helpers. `eligible_approvers` builds `EligibleSet.members` from `resolver.holders(...)` (role-grant/`user_role` based) and its exclusion filter joins `user_role`, but `_step` and `get_instance` then map those same ids through `_people`, which filters on the separate `identity_membership` table. `ordered = sorted(people[m.user_id] for m in eligible.members)` (line 340, mirrored at line 347) is an unguarded subscript: any permission holder lacking an `identity_membership` row falls out of `people` and raises KeyError. This is the "duplicated helper" drift the milestone asks reviewers to catch — `_people` is not the same membership predicate as the rest of the approval path.
findings.fix: Make the live-membership lookup one helper with one predicate (either resolve names/emails by id without the membership filter, as `emails_by_id`/`names_by_id` already do, or key `_people` off the same source `eligible_approvers`-uses), and let the mapping degrade gracefully instead of subscripting.
